video.title: Gemini 4 Argon - Full Tutorial: How To Build an App In Minutes

summary: Mikey (Mikey No Code) builds 'Lumen', an AI journaling web app, in Base44 using Google's Gemini 4 Argon across six layered prompts: liquid-glass design and core screens, organisation features, AI reflections and chat, authentication, a Stripe premium tier (PIN-locked entries, mood insights), and a UX polish pass, then tests the full new-user journey. The point is that coherence across many prompts, not the first impressive prompt, is the real test. The video repeatedly promotes his 'normally $499' Base44 masterclass, offered free. No revenue or distribution is covered.

tactics.name: Build an AI app in layered prompts, not one prompt
steps: Prompt 1: design system (liquid glass) and core screens with database; explicitly defer tags, search, AI, accounts, payments
Prompt 2: organisation features (tags, favourites, search, filters, calendar, streaks)
Prompt 3: built-in AI features (reflect, daily prompt, assistant chat with retry)
Prompt 4: authentication and per-user data isolation; publish to test
Prompt 5: Stripe test-mode premium with locked features and blurred previews
Prompt 6: global design/UX polish pass (empty states, loading, mobile)
Run a full new-user test on the published app

lessons.lesson: Explicitly defer features in prompts to keep the AI focused.
Use platform-native auth, AI and payments instead of building from scratch.
Gate premium features with visible previews to drive upgrades.
Do a final whole-app UX pass for empty states, loading and readability.
